Most of the merchantable saw timber is located along the drainages and north facing slopes where the moisture and temperature is most favorable for growth. Saw timber includes trees 9 inches or greater in diameter at breast height. Well stocked saw timber yields 8,500 board-feet per acre (bF/a.), medium stocked has 4500 bF/a. and poor stocked has 1000 bF/a. A low intensity survey was made of Tract III and it was estimated that the woodlands on this tract averaged 3300 bf/a, placing it in the low-medium category.
The ponderosa pine forest varies from sparsely stocked savanna type stands to overstocked "doghair" thickets. Data complied by Westmoreland Resources (1975 o) indicates that the density of the pine overstory varied from approximately 40 to 80 trees per acre on Tract II and from III to 1,381 trees per acre on Tract III, generally reaching the greatest density on north facing slopes. Tree age ranged from 23 to 138 years on Tract II and from 17 to 106 years on Tract III. Diameter at breast height (DBH) of trees averaged approximately 10 inches (25.4 cm) on Tract II while on Tract III the mean DBH was approximately 6 inches (15.2 cm).
Inventory data pertaining to volume, stocking, growth, etc. on the lease area are unavailable. Therefore data applicable to comparable forest stands near the Project Area has been used to make approximations.
